# Problem 1

"Load a dataset into R, gate it however you like, and then export out a population of interest as their own .fcs files. Open them in either Floreada.io or the commercial software of your choice, and take a screenshot of how they look by two markers of interest."


## Setup

Let's load some test files in the environment:

```{r}
#| eval: FALSE

# activate libraries:

library(flowWorkspace)
library(flowGate)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(purrr)

# get or set working directory:

getwd()

file_path = file.path("homeworkdata")

#list files:

fcs_files = list.files(file_path, pattern=".fcs", full.names=TRUE)
fcs_files


#load files in a cytoset:

CFC_cytoset = load_cytoset_from_fcs(fcs_files, truncate_max_range = FALSE, transformation = FALSE)
str(CFC_cytoset)

#create a gatingset:

CFC_GatingSet = GatingSet(CFC_cytoset)

# extract the column names which are the parameters inside the gating set
CFC_Parameters = colnames(CFC_GatingSet)
CFC_Parameters
```

The data I'm using was acquired in a conventional cytometer and I had DAPI as live/dead differentiator and these cells were transduced with a mock vector (GFP) and a treatment vector. 

Before I continue I will explore the FCS file with code from week 03 to see if I have any useful information about these files:


```{r}
#| eval: FALSE

firstfile = fcs_files[1]
firstfile
read.FCS(filename=firstfile)
flowFrame = read.FCS(filename=firstfile, transformation = FALSE, truncate_max_range = FALSE)
MFI_Matrix <- flowFrame@exprs
MFI_Matrix
ParameterData <- flowFrame@parameters@data

head(ParameterData, 10)

markers = markernames(CFC_GatingSet)
markers

```

So now I know that in my files I have the following channel/fluorochrome combinations: DAPI for viability, APC with MHC-I, APC-Cy7 with CD45 and GFP for GFP, PerCP-Cy5.5 was used as an empty channel for autofluorescence and gating strategy.


Before I gate these files, I will go back to week 07 lesson and play with transformation a bit to optimize visualization:


```{r}
#| eval: FALSE


# remove scatters and time parameters from the parameters column:
FluorophoresOnly = CFC_Parameters[!stringr::str_detect(CFC_Parameters, "FSC|SSC|Time")]
FluorophoresOnly

#preparing bioexponential transformation (copypasted from week07 homework)
Biexponential <- flowjo_biexp_trans() #default values

#Biexponential <- flowjo_biexp_trans(channelRange=4096, maxValue=262144,pos=4.5, neg=0, widthBasis=-1000) # width at -1000

#Biexponential <- flowjo_biexp_trans(channelRange=4096, maxValue=262144/2,pos=4.5, neg=0, widthBasis=-1000) # width and maxvalue changed:

#Biexponential = flowjo_biexp_trans(channelRange=4096, maxValue=262144, pos=4.5, neg=2, widthBasis=-500)

# attribute the bioexponential transformation to the fluorophores of interest (in this case all)
MyBiexTransform = transformerList(FluorophoresOnly, Biexponential)


#  apply the transformation to gating set:
transform(CFC_GatingSet, MyBiexTransform)

# plot the flow plot for one file:
ggcyto(CFC_GatingSet[4], subset="root",
 aes(x="APC-A", y="GFP-A")) + geom_hex(bins=100)

ggcyto(CFC_GatingSet[2], subset="root",
 aes(x="APC-A", y="GFP-A")) + geom_hex(bins=100)
```

Then I will create some gates using flowGate package and a tibble:

With this I can design a new gating strategy that makes sense:


```{r}

GatingTable = tibble::tribble(
  ~filterId,    ~dims,                          ~subset,      
  "singlets",   list("FSC-A", "FSC-H"),          "root",      
  "live",       list("FSC-A", "DAPI-A"),        "singlets",

)


#apply the gating strategy using gs_apply_gating_strategy:
```

I also know my metadata is quite empty. So I will alter it to include a few more details that could be useful for downstream analysis:

```{r}
#| eval: FALSE

metadata = pData(CFC_GatingSet)
str(metadata)

# Create a column with the timepoint, remove everything except D5 from the name

testing = metadata |> mutate(Timepoint = name)

testing = testing |> mutate(Timepoint = sub("^[^_]*_([^_]*)_.*$", "\\1", testing$Timepoint))


testing$Timepoint
## replace D5 for 5

testing = testing |> mutate(Timepoint = sub("D5", "5", testing$Timepoint))

testing

# create a column "condition" and remove all characters except the condition

testing = testing |> mutate(Condition = name)
testing = testing |> mutate(Condition = sub("^[^_]*_[^_]*_([^_]*)_.*$", "\\1", testing$Condition))

testing

# create a column called cell line and remove all characters except the first before the first underscore

testing = testing |> mutate(Cell_Line = name)

testing = testing |> mutate(Cell_Line = sub("_.*", "", testing$Cell_Line))

testing

metadata = testing

head(metadata, 4)

#replace the original metadata for the updated one

pData(CFC_GatingSet) = metadata

pData(CFC_GatingSet)

plot(CFC_GatingSet)
```

```{r}

downsampling_path
```

# Problem 2

"In the example for Downsampling() we only changed one keyword (GUID), after substituting in our desired addon right before the .fcs. Since keyword use might vary by manufacturer, create a couple additional arguments for Downsampling() that allow you to change out the values for some additional keywords."


## Solution

Adding a concatenation date as a keyword to the files created:


```{r}
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: FALSE

#' This function downsamples from a designated gate to our desired number
#' of cells, returning as a new .fcs file
#' 
#' @param x A GatingSet object, typically iterated in.
#' 
#' @param gate The gate from which to retrieve cell counts from 
#' 
#' @param inverse Whether to revert values back to their
#' original untransformed values before export as an .fcs file, default
#' is set to TRUE
#' 
#' @param DownsampleCount The desired number of cells to downsample from
#' each gated population. If value is less than 1, subsets out the 
#' equivalent proportion from that specimen
#' 
#' @param addon An additional character value to add before .fcs in the GUID
#' keyword to tell the downsampled file apart from the original. 
#' 
#' @param StorageLocation A file.path to the folder you want to store the new downsampled
#' 
#' fcs file to. Default NULL results in .fcs file being stored in current working directory
#' 
#' @param returnType Whether to return as a "fcs" file (default), or "flowFrame" or "data.frame"
#' 
#' 
#' @param Date adds a keyword with the concatenation date, preferably YYMMDD
#' 
#' 
Downsampling_1 <- function(x, gate, inverse=TRUE, DownsampleCount,
  addon, StorageLocation=NULL, returnType="fcs", Date){


EventsInTheGate = gs_pop_get_data(x, gate, inverse.transform = inverse)
  Exprs_data = exprs(EventsInTheGate[[1]])
  Exprs_data_frame = as.data.frame(Exprs_data, check.names = FALSE)

  if (DownsampleCount < 1){
    count = nrow(EventsInTheGate) # Original Count
    count = as.numeric(count) #Sanity Check on Value Type
    count = count*DownsampleCount # Target Cells
    count = round(count, 0) #rounded without decimals
    DownsampleCount = count # Over-writting DownsampleCount used for downsampling
  }

  downsample_data_frame = slice_sample(Exprs_data_frame, n = DownsampleCount, replace = FALSE) 
  
  downsample_matrix = as.matrix(downsample_data_frame)

  flowFrame = EventsInTheGate[[1, returnType="flowFrame"]]
  Original_parameters = parameters(flowFrame)
  Original_keywords = keyword(flowFrame)

  original_name = Original_keywords$GUID #gets the original name from GUID

  updated_name = paste0("_", addon, ".fcs") # adds between addon between _ and .fcs

  updated_GUID = sub(".fcs", updated_name, original_name) 
  
  #Switching out .fcs for Updated Name via the sub function
  Original_keywords$GUID = updated_GUID # OVERWRITING THE original keyword with the new one

  #adding a new keyword to the keyword list:

  new_keyword = list(ConcatDate = Date)

  Original_keywords = c(Original_keywords, new_keyword)
  
  
  new_fcs = new("flowFrame", exprs=downsample_matrix, parameters=Original_parameters, description=Original_keywords)

  if (is.null(StorageLocation)){
    StorageLocation <- getwd()}

  StorageLocation = file.path(StorageLocation, updated_GUID)


if (returnType == "fcs"){
    write.FCS(new_fcs, filename = StorageLocation, delimiter="#") # Write out .fcs file inside the storage location provided
  } else if (returnType == "data.frame"){
    return(downsample_data_frame) #Return data.frame without metadata changes (no keywords or parameters)
  } else {
    return(new_fcs) #All other criterias return a flowFrame with metadata
    }
}
```


let's see if it works in a gatingset with three files:


```{r}
#| eval: FALSE 

#get the folder path where the files are:
file_paths = file.path("data")

#get the fcs files full paths, hence full.names = TRUE
fcs_files = list.files(file_paths, pattern="Tcells.fcs", full.names=TRUE)
files = c(fcs_files[1], fcs_files[4], fcs_files[7])


#load the files into a cytoset:
SFC_cytoset = load_cytoset_from_fcs(files, truncate_max_range = FALSE, transformation = FALSE)

#load the cytoset into a gatingset:
SFC_GatingSet = GatingSet(SFC_cytoset)

# extract the column names which are the parameters inside the gating set
SFC_Parameters = colnames(SFC_GatingSet)

# remove scatters and time parameters from the parameters column:
FluorophoresOnly = SFC_Parameters[!stringr::str_detect(SFC_Parameters, "FSC|SSC|Time")]


#create the bioexponential transformation
Biexponential = flowjo_biexp_trans(channelRange=4096, maxValue=262144,
     pos=4.5, neg=2, widthBasis=-500)

# attribute the bioexponential transformation to the fluorophores of interest (in this case all)
MyBiexTransform = transformerList(FluorophoresOnly, Biexponential)


# apply the transformation to the gating set
transform(SFC_GatingSet, MyBiexTransform)

#  Gating strategy:


GatingTable = tibble::tribble(
  ~filterId,    ~dims,                          ~subset,      
  "singlets",   list("FSC-A", "FSC-H"),          "root",      
  "live",       list("FSC-A", "Zombie NIR-A"),   "singlets",  
  "Tcells",     list("CD3", "CD45"),             "live",     
  "CD4+",       list("CD8", "CD4"),              "Tcells",   
  "CD8+",       list("CD8", "CD4"),              "Tcells",   
  "DN",         list("CD8", "CD4"),              "Tcells",  
)


#apply the gating strategy using gs_apply_gating_strategy:

gs_apply_gating_strategy(SFC_GatingSet, gating_strategy = GatingTable)


#look at the overall structure of the gating strategy:

plot(SFC_GatingSet)

ggcyto::autoplot(SFC_GatingSet[[1]]) + theme_bw()
```


So after having the gating set ready I can downsample the files into CD8+ only:



```{r}
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: FALSE


purrr::walk(.x=SFC_GatingSet, gate="CD8+", .f=Downsampling_1, DownsampleCount=2500, addon="onlyCD8", returnType="fcs", Date= 260723, StorageLocation = file_path)
```
